sections.html:
Oak Forest sellers deal with Cook County recording and a handful of city programs for rentals, vacant buildings and code upkeep. The city's own rules are light for an owner-occupied house, but a former rental or empty property brings extra registration questions.

The city sits about 24 miles south-southwest of downtown Chicago in Bremen Township and has 26,792 residents (July 2025 estimate). Median owner-occupied value is $255,100, 82.4% of homes are owner-occupied, and 92.0% of residents lived in the same house a year earlier. Start with three questions: who holds title, whether anyone has rented the house, and whether any code notice is open. Those answers decide how long the sale takes.

The Cook County Clerk's municipal transfer tax list has no line for Oak Forest, though it does list nearby suburbs such as Oak Lawn, Worth, Midlothian and Country Club Hills. The Clerk adds that buyers of stamps should confirm with the municipality, so call City Hall at 708-687-4050 before closing.

The state and county taxes apply to every Cook County sale, with the seller liable. The state rate is set by 35 ILCS 200/31-10, and the PTAX-203 declaration accompanies the deed.

Oak Forest regulates rentals more closely than many suburbs, so a house that was ever leased may carry a registration trail.

  • All rental properties must be registered under the Crime Free Multi-Housing ordinance, with a license for each calendar year. The fee is $100 for one to five units, $150 for six to ten, and rises to $500 for 41 or more.
  • Landlords complete a seminar, a physical security inspection, background checks for new tenants age 18 and over, and a city lease addendum. Missing records can bring a fine of up to $750.
  • Apartment and condominium buildings are registered and inspected every year, with inspections from May 1 through September 30.
  • Vacant buildings must be registered, with a $700 fee and required inspections.
  • A short-term vacation rental license costs $50 a year, requires the owner to live in the home as a primary residence for nine of twelve months, and requires $1,000,000 per occurrence in liability insurance.

Foreclosure notices and confirmation orders go to the city's Property Maintenance Coordinator at 15440 S. Central Avenue, and code questions go to Property Maintenance at 708-444-4846. Ask the Crime Free Housing office at 708-687-4050 extension 1295 whether a rental license is current.

The city enforces the 2018 International Property Maintenance Code with local amendments. Violation notices cite the problem, set a correction date and schedule a re-inspection, and unresolved items can bring fines.

  • Typical violations include rubbish, tall grass, inoperable or unlicensed vehicles, roof and fence repair, and grading and drainage.
  • House numbers must be at least four inches high and plainly visible from the street.
  • Recreational vehicles of 26 feet or less may be stored anywhere on a lot, those between 26 and 40 feet only in a side or rear yard, and vehicles of 40 feet or more are not permitted.

Clear any open notice before listing. It is easier to settle before a buyer's inspector sees it.

sections.h2: Recording and closing in Cook County
sections.html:
An Oak Forest deed is recorded with the Cook County Clerk's recordings office at 118 N. Clark St., phone 312.603.5050. A rubber stamp is the proof of payment, and municipal amounts vary by location.

  • Bring a signed deed and the PTAX-203 declaration, or an exemption statement if the transfer is not a sale.
  • Pay or settle any final water bill with the city before the closing date.
  • If the house is in a trust or an estate, give the title company the trust certificate or letters of office early.
  • Say whether the property is a single-family house, condominium or multi-unit building, since the city registers each type differently.

Oak Forest sits in Bremen Township, one of the south and west suburb townships on the Cook County Assessor's triennial reassessment cycle. The Bremen township assessor takes inquiries by appointment at 708-333-1591. The Assessor's PIN search is needed for a building permit or an appeal.

Ask the Cook County Treasurer for the balance and installment status on the parcel, and ask the title company how the closing statement will prorate that year's bill.

Public elementary districts include Forest Ridge District 142, Arbor Park District 145 and Tinley Park District 146. Oak Forest High School is part of Bremen District 228, and parts of the city feed Tinley Park, Victor J. Andrew or Carl Sandburg high schools, so confirm by address.

US Route 6 (159th Street) and Illinois Route 50 (Cicero Avenue) are the main crossing roads, and Interstate 57 clips the southeast corner. The Oak Forest Metra station at 159th and Cicero is on the Rock Island District line to LaSalle Street, and Pace routes 354, 364 and 383 serve the city. The mean commute is 31.8 minutes, so train access and quick reach to I-57 are worth stating in a listing.

A traditional listing suits an updated house with no open notices. A direct sale to a cash buyer suits a house that needs work, a rental with a messy license history, or an inherited home where relatives live out of state. Both routes use the same Cook County recording steps.

Before you choose, check the three things buyers' attorneys ask about first: open code notices, any rental or vacancy registration, and the water account. A clean answer on each shortens the closing, and a problem on any of them is easier to solve before you sign a contract.

sections.h2: Paperwork to gather before you list
sections.html:
Collect the deed or trust documents, your latest Cook County tax bill, and any payoff statement. If the house was ever rented, pull the rental license record and ask the Crime Free Housing office whether your registration is current. If the building was ever empty, ask Property Maintenance whether a vacant building registration was filed and whether the $700 fee was paid.

Walk the exterior as an inspector would: house numbers, tall grass, vehicles, fences, roof and drainage. Fix or document anything that could draw a notice. Then call City Hall at 708-687-4050 to confirm there is no municipal transfer stamp for your address, and call the water office so the final bill is settled before closing.

faqs.q: Does Oak Forest have a municipal transfer tax?
faqs.a: The Cook County Clerk's list shows no Oak Forest tax, but the Clerk tells buyers to confirm with the municipality. Call City Hall at 708-687-4050 to be sure. State and county transfer taxes still apply.

faqs.q: Do I need to register a rental before selling it?
faqs.a: Oak Forest requires every rental property to be registered each calendar year, with fees by unit count. Ask the Crime Free Housing office at 708-687-4050 extension 1295 whether your license is current.

faqs.q: What is the fee for vacant property registration?
faqs.a: The city charges a $700 registration fee for a vacant building and requires inspections. The owner or anyone with a legal or equitable interest must register it.
Oak Forest is in Bremen Township, on the south and west suburban reassessment cycle. Look up your PIN on the Cook County Assessor's site to confirm.

Elementary districts include 142, 145 and 146, and Oak Forest High School is part of Bremen District 228. Parts of the city feed Tinley Park, Victor J. Andrew or Carl Sandburg high schools, so confirm by address.
